title: Cloud-scale molecular gas properties of the ANTENNAE merger: a comparative study with PHANGS-ALMA galaxies and NGC 3256
question: How do the cloud-scale molecular gas properties of the Antennae merger (NGC 4038/9) compare to those in nearby spiral galaxies from PHANGS-ALMA and the late-stage merger NGC 3256, and how do they depend on merger stage?

data.angular_resolution: 0.51 arcsec (55 pc) native; also convolved to 80, 90, 120, and 150 pc

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image interferometric and Total Power CO (2-1) data and combine across spatial scales
recipe.method: Reapply ALMA observatory pipeline calibration to 12 m and 7 m data, subtract continuum, jointly image and clean both 12 m configurations and 7 m ACA using modified PHANGS-ALMA pipeline (multi-scale then single-scale tclean), calibrate/image TP data with PHANGS-ALMA TP pipeline, correct for primary beam, convolve to circular beams (55, 80, 90, 120, 150 pc), feather interferometric and TP cubes, and regrid pixels to half beam FWHM.
software: PHANGS-ALMA TP calibration and imaging pipeline
key_parameters: Multi-scale clean scales: point sources, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, and 10 arcsec
Circular synthesized beam FWHMs: 55, 80, 90, 120, and 150 pc

recipe.goal: Calculate moment maps and derive pixel-by-pixel cloud-scale molecular gas properties
recipe.method: Calculate moment 0, 1, and 2 maps and peak brightness temperature (T_B,max) following Brunetti et al. (2021). Convert integrated intensity to molecular gas mass surface density (Sigma_mol) using a constant Milky Way conversion factor, and compute virial parameter (alpha_vir) and internal turbulent pressure (P_turb/k_B) in each Nyquist-sampled square pixel using Equations 1 and 2.
assumptions: 12CO J=2-1 / J=1-0 line ratio = 0.70 and Milky Way conversion factor (including helium and heavy elements) applies across NGC 4038/9
A single cloud roughly fills each synthesized beam and cloud density profile follows rho(r) proportional to r^-1

recipe.goal: Separate pixel measurements into regional sub-samples and compare statistical distributions across galaxies
recipe.method: Divide pixels into nuclear (< 1 kpc from either nucleus), non-nuclear (> 1 kpc), and Whitmore et al. (2014) CO (3-2) overlap region FoV sub-samples. Apply the same 1 kpc nuclear separation to PHANGS-ALMA galaxies. Compute mass-weighted medians, inner 68th percentiles, and 1D/2D Gaussian kernel density estimators (KDEs) to compare NGC 4038/9 with NGC 3256 and 70 PHANGS-ALMA galaxies.
key_parameters: Gaussian KDE bandwidth selection: Scott's Rule
